findings.title: Fixed-host override checks allow slots that extend outside the override window
findings.body: The override predicate only rejects a slot when its end is at/before the override start or its start is after the override end. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it, or starts inside it and ends after it, matches neither condition and is treated as available. For a round-robin event this can expose a slot whose fixed host is unavailable for part of the booking duration; the check needs to require the entire [slot start, slot end] interval to be contained in an override range.

findings.title: Multiple date-override ranges on one day are treated as an intersection
findings.body: `dateOverrides.find` returns an unavailable result as soon as any same-day override does not contain the slot. With two valid availability windows on a day (for example 09:00-10:00 and 14:00-15:00), a slot inside the first window is rejected by the second window, and vice versa. Date overrides represent alternative available ranges, so a fixed host should be available when the slot is contained in any matching override, not every override.

findings.title: All-day date overrides are never recognized as equal start/end times
findings.body: This compares two separately-created Dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false even when `date.start` and `date.end` represent the same instant. Consequently an all-day/unavailable override skips the intended special case and can leave a slot beginning exactly at the override timestamp available (typically the first slot at midnight). Use a value comparison such as `isSame` or compare timestamps.

findings.title: Working-hours validation ignores the booking end time
findings.body: `end` is calculated from `slotStartTime` exactly like `start`, rather than from `slotEndTime`. Therefore any slot that starts before a fixed/loose host's working-hours end passes this check even if the event extends beyond that host's availability. This can make round-robin slots bookable when a required fixed host cannot attend the full event.

findings.title: The added regression test does not cover the fixed-host round-robin behavior being changed
findings.body: The new timezone assertion uses a personal event with `hosts: []`, so it never executes the fixed-host filtering path added in `checkIfIsAvailable`. There is no test with a ROUND_ROBIN event, at least one `isFixed: true` host, and that host's date override; regressions that again expose unavailable fixed-host slots would not be caught.
